M-2.0.title: Home
M-2.0.note: The three suggestion chips under “How are you feeling today?” are different demo stories — tap them one by one to walk a real chat, then follow into Visit Notes after an answer. Typing free text works too. From here you can also open My Health, My Notes, labs, or the Wellness Plan card when one exists.

M-1.1.title: Splash
M-1.1.note: A first-time user has just opened the app. This is a short brand moment, about 3 seconds, while the app 'loads'. It should feel calm and trustworthy. It fades into Welcome. Returning users who already consented skip it and land in Main.

M-1.2.title: Welcome
M-1.2.note: Maria meets the Oracle for the first time. The aim is a warm, human first contact that asks only for her first name and makes clear she is talking to an AI. Get started accepts the terms and opens her first conversation. Sign in is there for returning users.

M-1.3.title: Before we begin (consent)
M-1.3.note: This is a calm, easy-to-scan summary of what the app is and isn't, plus the AI disclosure and the agreement checkbox. It was merged into Welcome on 2026-10-08, so it stays in the code but is no longer part of the flow. Agreeing opens the empty Conversation.

M-2.1.title: Conversation
M-2.1.note: This is the consultation. Suggestions and replies drive a scripted flow: light intake, then the Oracle’s answer, then What’s next. From What’s next you can open the Wellness Plan, upload labs, or move into Visit Notes. Try one Home suggestion all the way through to see the full path.

M-2.7.title: Shop (in-app browser)
M-2.7.note: Maria tapped a product from an answer, her 90-day plan or a piece of content. A mock Genesis Gold page opens in an in-app browser, labelled 'Formulated by Genesis Health Products', with ?ref=app. Shopping is a demo and checkout happens on the real site. Done takes her back to exactly where she was.

M-2.8.title: Follow-up opt-in
M-2.8.note: This sheet appears right after Maria's first completed answer. The Oracle offers to check in later so they can build on today. Maria picks a reminder interval. Our own friendly prompt always comes before the system permission alert. Not now dismisses it without any pressure.

M-4.1.title: Free limit reached
M-4.1.note: Maria has used her 3 free consultations and is trying to start a new one. The sheet tells her that her answers are saved and invites her to choose a plan. It should never feel like a trap: safety features keep working. It leads to Choose plan, or Maybe later.

M-4.2.title: Choose plan
M-4.2.note: Maria compares the Individual and Family plans, either monthly or annually. One plan is always preselected based on where she came from (for example, Family when she came from the upgrade sheet). Continue takes her to account creation if she has no account yet, or straight to payment.

M-4.3.title: Create account / Sign in
M-4.3.note: The account is created only at conversion, framed as 'Save your health history'. Maria can sign up with Apple, Google or email plus a verification code, and her trial history moves with her. In sign-in mode, opened from Welcome, it greets a returning user and takes them back to Main.

M-4.5.title: Plan success
M-4.5.note: The purchase is done. 'You're all set': unlimited consultations are unlocked and the trial counter disappears. Continue my conversation sends any message she had held back. Family plan users can go straight to adding a family member.

M-4.4.title: Store payment (simulated)
M-4.4.note: This is a mock of the App Store subscription sheet that confirms the plan, price and auto-renewal. It should feel familiar and trustworthy. Subscribe shows a short spinner, then Done, and moves on to the success screen. Cancel returns to Choose plan.

M-5.1.title: Lock screen notification
M-5.1.note: Weeks later, the Oracle reaches out with a generic nudge: 'How are you feeling this week?'. The lock screen never shows health details. Tapping it unlocks the phone and deep-links into a check-in conversation for the right profile. It is the moment that brings Maria back.

M-5.3.title: Add lab results
M-5.3.note: Upload or enter labs here (photo, PDF, or typed values). You’ll confirm the numbers on the next screen; the Oracle can then use them in chat. This is simulated reading — not real OCR.

M-5.4.title: Confirm lab results
M-5.4.note: Maria checks the values that were picked up from her report and can edit, add or delete any of them before sending. This gives her control and keeps the results accurate. Sending leads to a lab-informed answer in Conversation, and the report is saved to Records.

M-6.1.title: Profile switcher
M-6.1.note: 'Who is this for?' Maria can switch between herself and her family members, and each person keeps their own private history. Switching resets Ask and My Health to that person. From here she can add a member (or see the upgrade sheet if she isn't on the Family plan) or manage profiles.

M-6.2.title: Add family member
M-6.2.note: Maria adds someone, for example her teen daughter, with their name, relationship, date of birth, sex at birth and a consent confirmation. Children under 13 are blocked for now. Create profile switches to the new person and opens an empty conversation with teen-appropriate suggestions.

M-6.3.title: Upgrade to Family
M-6.3.note: Maria tried to add a family member but isn't on the Family plan. This light sheet explains that the plan covers up to 5 people, each with their own private history. Upgrade opens Choose plan with Family preselected, then returns her to adding the member. Not now dismisses it.

M-6.5.title: Profile details
M-6.5.note: This shows one person's basics and the health info gathered from intake, all editable, with links to their consultations, Visit Notes and labs. For profiles other than Maria's own, there is also a clearly destructive delete option. It reassures her that each profile's data is separate and under her control.

M-6.6.title: Manage profiles
M-6.6.note: This is a simple list of every profile with a count out of 5, reached from the switcher or from Account. Each row opens Profile details, and there is a row to add a family member. It isn't in the wireframes; this is the minimal version from the spec.

M-7.1.title: My Health (empty)
M-7.1.note: The active profile hasn't completed a consultation yet. The hub is never blank: it explains that her health picture builds as she talks with the Oracle and offers popular starting points. Start my first consultation opens the Ask tab. The hub fills in automatically after her first answer.

M-7.2.title: My Health hub
M-7.2.note: This person’s health home between chats. The Wellness Plan card opens the living plan. Check-in and health profile sit underneath. Tap the plan card to see concerns, actions, and the Oracle’s letter.

M-7.3.title: Your Wellness Plan
M-7.3.note: This is the living Wellness Plan. Newest concern stays open at the top; earlier ones stay collapsed underneath. Check off actions in the wells — that only tracks progress, it does not close the concern. Tap “This concern is resolved” and confirm when that topic is done; the name stays under Resolved. The clinical letter below is the Oracle’s standing reference.

M-7.4.title: Content detail
M-7.4.note: Maria opens a video or article the Oracle picked for her, with a line explaining why she is seeing it. Ask Oracle about this takes her into chat with the composer already filled in, so learning turns into conversation. A related product, if there is one, opens the shop.

M-7.5.title: The Oracle's library
M-7.5.note: Maria can browse all of the Oracle's content: search it, filter by For you, All or New, or by topic. Empty results gently send her to ask the Oracle directly. This screen also links to the Facebook community and to About the Oracle.

M-7.6.title: About the Oracle
M-7.6.note: This screen tells Maria who is behind the app: Deborah's portrait, credentials, philosophy and books. Its job is to build trust in the real person. The main action is Book a consultation with Deborah. The bio and photography are placeholders until Deborah approves them.

M-8.2.title: Booking info
M-8.2.note: When the app isn't enough, Maria can reach the support team herself. This screen explains what to expect from the 50-minute video visit, asks which state she lives in (for licensing) and offers an opt-in to share her app history. Choose a time leads to the scheduler. The price is still to be decided.

M-8.3.title: Scheduler
M-8.3.note: Maria picks a day and an available slot. This is a simulated, native-feeling scheduler. A summary bar confirms her choice, and Confirm booking books it, sets a reminder for the day before and replaces this screen with the confirmation.

M-8.4.title: Booking confirmed
M-8.4.note: 'Booked with the Oracle', with the date, time and a promise of a reminder the day before. Maria should feel looked after. She can add the visit to her calendar, view details (with a cancel option) or go back to chat. The booking also appears in her hub.

M-9.1.title: My Notes
M-9.1.note: Saved consultations, Visit Notes, and labs for this person. Open an old visit note to reread it, or start logging what changed after a provider visit. Labs here can be opened or asked about in chat.

M-9.2.title: Consultation detail
M-9.2.note: Maria rereads a past consultation: the transcript, the collapsed intake summary and the Oracle's full 7-section answer. She can download a PDF to bring to her provider, share it, or continue the chat, which reopens that conversation and the Oracle remembers it.

M-9.4.title: Note editor
M-9.4.note: Maria writes down questions before a visit, notes after a visit, or a saved answer. Question notes render as a checklist. Notes save automatically, so nothing gets lost. It isn't in the wireframes, and it's still open whether the Oracle may read these notes later.

M-9.5.title: Lab report
M-9.5.note: A saved lab report. Ask Oracle about these labs to pull them into a conversation so she has the numbers as context. You can also edit or delete from the menu.

M-9.6.title: PDF preview
M-9.6.note: Printable summary for a clinician. When the conversation has enough detail (Miro Step 5), this shows the full My Visit Notes brief; otherwise a shorter questions-and-tests page. Share and Print are simulated. Plan gating is still open; the prototype allows it for everyone.

M-9.7.title: My Visit Notes
M-9.7.note: A note to take to a clinician. Save a copy into Visit Notes, or download the PDF preview. After a real appointment, come back here or log what changed on the after-visit form.

M-9.8.title: Log your visit
M-9.8.note: Log what the provider said, tests ordered, and medication changes. Kind of provider is required before Save — leave it blank to see the gate. Open an older visit note from My Notes to reread what was already logged.

M-10.1.title: Account
M-10.1.note: This is one calm place for Maria's plan, family profiles, notifications, privacy, legal and About the Oracle. Trial users see a Choose a plan card at the top. Sign out keeps her data in her account and returns her to Welcome.

M-10.2.title: Privacy & data
M-10.2.note: This is where Maria exercises her data rights: download her data, read how it is used (never for training without consent), delete a profile, or delete her account. Deleting the account takes deliberate steps, including typing DELETE, and then resets the app. It should feel transparent and respectful.

M-10.3.title: Subscription
M-10.3.note: This shows Maria's current plan, price and renewal date. She can change plan, manage it in the App Store, or cancel; the plan stays active until the renewal date. It isn't in the wireframes.

M-10.4.title: Notifications
M-10.4.note: Maria controls check-in reminders (and how often they come) and booking reminders. A note reassures her that health details never show on her lock screen. If system permission is off, a banner offers a way to fix it. It isn't in the wireframes.

M-10.5.title: Terms & disclaimer
M-10.5.note: This is a read-only view of the Terms & Disclaimer, the privacy notice and the AI disclosure, showing which version Maria accepted and when. It opens from Welcome, from the (i) menu and from Account. All the copy is placeholder until the attorney drafts it.

M-11.1.title: Documents and reports
M-11.1.note: Upload documents and reports here, or open one you already saved. You can bring a document into chat later so the Oracle has that context when she answers.

M-11.3.title: Upload a document
M-11.3.note: Add a document now. It lands in Documents; from there you can ask the Oracle about it in chat so she answers with that file in mind. Upload is simulated in the prototype.
